counterparty.name: SFJ Pharmaceuticals X, Ltd. (SFJ)
counterparty.role: co-developer, clinical-trial support provider, and funder

items.expectedFix: Add a mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees or analogous amounts paid or payable, with uncapped carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; preferably also carve out data protection/security, fraud and IP infringement.
items.note: The agreement mutually excludes indirect, consequential and similar damages, but contains no aggregate liability cap. PB's direct liability is therefore uncapped, and the exclusion applies broadly to indemnity and negligence without the required carve-outs.

items.expectedFix: Expand SFJ's indemnity to cover third-party IP claims arising from SFJ services or materials, SFJ's breach of law, SFJ-caused data breaches, and SFJ's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with any Customer indemnity appropriately limited.
items.note: SFJ indemnifies PB for SFJ's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, material breach and protocol breaches, with standard claim procedures. It does not expressly cover infringement caused by SFJ's services or materials, breach of law, or a data breach caused by SFJ, while PB gives SFJ a broad product and IP indemnity.
The defined-product non-compete binds SFJ and its affiliates, not PB. It therefore benefits the Customer side and is not a Customer restriction.

This provision requires SFJ to seek an assignment or licence of contractor-created Trial Inventions for PB. It is an IP-rights provision benefiting PB, not an exclusive-purchasing or sole-supplier obligation binding PB.
No most-favoured-nation obligation requires PB to extend SFJ terms offered to third parties.

items.expectedFix: Confirm and cap the restriction at 12 months after the employee's involvement ends, and expressly exclude unsolicited approaches in addition to general solicitations.
items.note: The restriction is mutual, limited to personnel involved in the development activities, and contains a general-advertising carve-out. The post-term duration is redacted, so it cannot be determined whether it is within the 12-month fallback or exceeds the permitted period.

items.expectedFix: Permit PB to terminate on 30 days' notice, or at most 60–90 days, without the funding threshold and with any early-termination fee capped at three months' fees or comparable charges.
items.note: PB has an at-will termination right only after SFJ has funded or incurred $60 million and before the first Regulatory Approval. Exercise requires a redacted notice period and a payment equal to 300% of SFJ's Development Costs, far exceeding the permitted fallback termination fee.
The agreement expires upon termination or payment of the final Approval Payment and does not automatically renew.

items.expectedFix: Retain Delaware law but provide for exclusive Delaware state and federal courts, or adopt New York law with exclusive New York County courts.
items.note: Delaware governing law is acceptable, but most disputes are subject to mandatory ICDR arbitration seated in New York rather than courts in an accepted jurisdiction. This does not reach the stated Delaware-law-and-courts fallback.

items.expectedFix: Permit PB to assign the relevant payment rights to affiliates and M&A or asset-sale successors, with notice and appropriate assumption or guarantee obligations.
items.note: The general assignment clause permits affiliate and M&A-successor assignments and restricts SFJ's transfer to pharmaceutical or biotechnology entities without PB's consent. However, PB is separately prohibited from assigning royalty or licence-fee receivables except to a wholly owned subsidiary, without an M&A-successor carve-out.

items.expectedFix: Delete SFJ's change-of-control termination right. A permitted PB successor should assume the agreement, subject only to reasonable notice and credit-support requirements.
items.note: Although PB receives a favorable optional change-of-control buy-out right, SFJ may terminate the entire agreement in its sole discretion following any qualifying Change of Control of PB before the final Approval Payment. This is an impermissible counterparty termination right triggered by Customer change of control.

PB retains its existing IP, owns all Trial Inventions regardless of inventorship, and acquires sole ownership of the Trial Data Package, Research Results and relevant Product Filings. Assignments to MedImmune concern IP governed by PB's upstream AZ License and do not transfer PB-owned data or deliverables to SFJ.

If assignment from an SFJ consultant cannot be obtained, SFJ must secure for PB an exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid, freely assignable licence with multi-tier sublicensing rights and rights covering all uses of the Product. This exceeds the transferability fallback.

The cited provisions concern PB's own quality audits of manufacturing or third-party facilities and periodic financial reporting or executive discussions. They do not grant SFJ unlimited, unannounced, or direct-system audit access against PB.

items.expectedFix: Delete the cost multipliers and 25% interest component. Limit any convenience-termination charge to three months' fees, and for breach permit only demonstrable direct losses subject to the negotiated liability framework.
items.note: PB must make stipulated termination payments in several circumstances, including amounts equal to 150% or 300% of SFJ's Development Costs and, in one case, Development Costs plus 25% annual interest. Section 14.4.2 treats the specified termination payments as replacing SFJ's damages claim, making them functionally liquidated damages or penalties far above the permitted fallback.

items.expectedFix: Add an SFJ warranty that services will be performed professionally, workmanlike, in accordance with applicable law and agreed specifications, with at least a 30-day services warranty and re-performance or refund remedies.
items.note: No express warranty requires SFJ's services to be performed professionally and workmanlike or provides a repair, re-performance, replacement or refund remedy.

items.expectedFix: Require SFJ to maintain E&O coverage of at least $1 million and cyber/privacy coverage of at least $2 million, with disclosed limits, certificates on request, and appropriate post-termination coverage.
items.note: The agreement requires mutual CGL, umbrella, clinical-trial and product-liability coverage, certificates on request, and professional liability for subcontractors. Limits are redacted, SFJ itself is not clearly required to maintain E&O coverage, and no cyber/privacy insurance is required despite processing clinical-trial personal data.

items.expectedFix: Delete the matching minimum-spend obligation or limit it to an approved 12-month budget that PB may reduce on 30 days' notice without penalty.
items.note: PB must spend at least an amount equal to all funding paid by SFJ under Section 4.2. This is a substantial minimum-spend commitment without a simple reduction right and can continue across the multi-year development arrangement.

items.expectedFix: Specify delivery of all data and filings in a standard usable format within 30 days, at least 90 days of transition assistance, and deletion certification after PB confirms successful transfer.
items.note: Upon termination, SFJ must transfer the Trial Data Package, Product Filings, clinical trials and relevant vendor agreements to PB and provide cooperation intended to avoid interruption. However, the periods for delivering the filings and continuing trial operations are redacted, so compliance with the 30-day export and 90-day transition fallback cannot be confirmed. Many CUAD-located spans concern termination payments rather than transition services.
